subject: Mathematics

Lab Practical (activities from the prescribed books)

textbooks: Guidelines for Mathematics Laboratory in Schools, class IX (CBSE)
Mathematics exemplar problems for class IX (NCERT)

chapters.name: Number System
topics: Representation of rational numbers on the number line
Density of rational numbers and its proof
Finding rational numbers between any two rational numbers
outcomes: Represents rational numbers on the number line
Explains the density of rational numbers
Computes decimal representations of rational numbers
Proves irrationality
Constructs the square root spiral

chapters.name: Introduction to Polynomials
topics: Definition and degree of a polynomial
Modelling linear growth and linear decay
Slope and y-intercept of a line y = ax + b
outcomes: Identifies the degree, terms and coefficients of a polynomial
Models linear growth and decay using linear polynomials
Identifies the slope and y-intercept of a linear equation in two variables
Graphs a linear equation in two variables

chapters.name: Sequences and Progressions
topics: Explicit (general) and recursive rules of a sequence
Arithmetic Progressions: nth term, visualising an AP, practical contexts
Sum of the first n natural numbers
Geometric Progressions: nth term, visualising a GP, practical contexts
outcomes: Determines recursive and explicit rules for sequences
Determines the nth term of an AP and of a GP
Visualises APs and GPs graphically
Analyses attributes of fractals using GP
Solves the Tower of Hanoi puzzle

chapters.name: Exploring Algebraic Identities
topics: Factorisation of algebraic expressions using identities
Visualising factorisation of quadratic expressions with and without algebra tiles
outcomes: Visualises algebraic identities using geometric models
Factors algebraic expressions using identities
Interprets factors of quadratic expressions through geometric models
Simplifies rational expressions

chapters.name: Linear Equations in Two Variables
topics: Linear equations in two variables through practical examples
Graphs when x and y assume only certain values
Pair of linear equations in two variables
Graphical method for solving a pair of linear equations
Nature of solutions: consistency and inconsistency
outcomes: Solves a pair of linear equations graphically and by substitution and elimination
Determines the nature of solutions of a pair of linear equations

chapters.name: Coordinate Geometry
topics: Distance between two points in the 2-D plane
Midpoint of the line segment between two points
outcomes: Specifies locations and relative positions using coordinates
Computes the distance between two points
Determines whether three points are collinear
Computes the midpoint of a line segment
Checks whether a triangle is right-angled using coordinates

chapters.name: Introduction to Euclid's Geometry: Axioms and Postulates
topics: Constructing a square with a given side as in Baudhayana's Sulbasutras
Axioms of measurement and rules for geometric objects
outcomes: Describes contributions of India, Egypt and Greece to geometry
Explains the role of definitions, axioms and postulates
States the five postulates of Euclidean geometry
Justifies simple constructions using the axioms

chapters.name: Lines and Angles
topics: Theorems and examples on intersecting lines
Theorems and examples on parallel lines
outcomes: Classifies angles as acute, right, obtuse or reflex
States and applies the linear pair theorem and its converse
Proves that vertically opposite angles are equal
Identifies corresponding, alternate and interior angles
Follows proof by contradiction in geometry

chapters.name: Triangles: Congruence Theorems
topics: Proofs of conditions of congruence of triangles
Problems based on applications of theorems on triangles
outcomes: Uses the SAS, SSS, ASA, RHS and AAS congruence conditions
Proves basic properties of isosceles triangles
Identifies the converse of a proposition and uses counter-examples

chapters.name: 4-gons (Quadrilaterals)
topics: Theorems related to parallelograms and their proof
Central symmetry in the context of parallelograms
outcomes: Proves characterisations of a parallelogram
Proves the midpoint theorem and a converse
Proves that the medians of a triangle are concurrent and divided in the ratio 2:1

chapters.name: Circles
topics: Practical applications and uses of circles
Chords and the angles they subtend
Midpoints and perpendicular bisectors of chords
Distance of chords from the centre
outcomes: Constructs the circumcircle and circumcentre of a triangle
Explains why equal chords subtend equal angles at the centre
Relates chord length to its distance from the centre
Explains that the angle at the centre is double the angle at the circumference
Determines when four points are concyclic
Explains that a quadrilateral with supplementary opposite angles is cyclic, and conversely

chapters.name: Area and Perimeter
topics: Perimeter of a circle: introduction to π and its irrationality
Area of rectangles, parallelograms and triangles
Squaring a rectangle: proof from Baudhayana's Sulbasutras
Area of the sector of a circle
Brahmagupta's formula for the area of a cyclic 4-gon

chapters.name: Surface Area and Volume
topics: Surface areas and volumes of spheres (including hemispheres) and right circular cones
outcomes: Computes surface area and volume of cuboids, cubes, cylinders, cones, pyramids and spheres

chapters.name: Statistics
outcomes: Collects, organises, visualises and interprets data to answer a statistical question
Computes and applies weighted averages
Reads and interprets stacked and 100% stacked bar graphs

chapters.name: Introduction to Probability
topics: Empirical probability: analysing data and performing experiments
Theoretical probability: sample space and events
Representing probability through tree diagrams and tables
outcomes: Describes the likelihood of an event on the probability scale
